attribution.note: Zitron's own words, in a passage he quotes from his own premium newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'because' link and the universal 'not a single'. The 'stress test' framing is a metaphor; the testable part is the premise.

contract.note: Plain reading is ordinary: a company already profitable, or one that later posts an operating profit, has a path to profitability. One counterexample is enough to break the universal. Whether one quarter counts as a 'path' is a fair ambiguity, but Gamma's multi-year profitability claim does not depend on it.

evidence.note: Yahoo Finance coverage of the S-1 (2026-10-26, before the cutoff): Anthropic had $974M Q2 2026 operating income.
Independent report that confirms the same S-1 Q2 operating profit figure.
Gamma, an AI-native app maker, said in Nov 2025 it had been profitable for over two years. Unaudited company disclosure, which the contract accepts.
Anthropic still had an H1 2026 operating loss of $693M. This limits how lasting its profit is, but does not undo the Q2 operating profit.

reviews.rationale: The premise is universal: not a single generative AI company has a path to profitability. Two companies break it. Gamma reported being profitable for over two years as of Nov 2025, and Anthropic's S-1 shows Q2 2026 operating profit before the evaluation date. Anthropic's H1 operating loss and the fact that Gamma's figures are self-reported weaken the evidence, but do not save the universal. The causal claim fails along with its premise.

semantics.note: Keeps the hyperscaler carve-out and the universal scope ('none', 'every single part').

contract.note: Plain reading (covering costs with outside capital rather than own revenue) is ordinary. Excluding indirect upstream subsidy is a judgment call, but counting it would make the claim true by definition. The 2025 window fits a present-tense claim.

evidence.note: OpenAI spent $34B against $13B revenue in 2025 and was funded by investors. Supports the model-provider link only, not the universal.
Gamma, a non-hyperscaler AI app company with $100M ARR, was profitable through 2025, so it was fueled by revenue. Self-reported.

reviews.rationale: The claim is universal: no part of the AI industry outside the hyperscaler carve-out is fueled by revenue. OpenAI's 2025 losses support it for the model-provider link. Gamma, a meaningful AI app company profitable through 2025 on its own revenue, is a counterexample under the contract's reading. The result depends on not treating below-cost upstream model pricing as subsidizing Gamma.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Rightly reduces the statement to its testable core: every AI app is subsidized and priced below cost. 'Lied to' and 'none of this is real' are rhetoric.

contract.note: Maker-level reading (price does not cover the maker's costs, with the gap filled by outside money) is an ordinary sense of 'subsidized'. The contract flags but does not settle the indirect-subsidy reading, and that reading would change the result.

evidence.note: Gamma says it was profitable for over two years as of Nov 2025, with little outside funding. Unaudited company disclosure with no figures.
Anthropic's compute cost was about 2.5x revenue in early 2025, so Claude was sold below cost then. One instance only; does not prove the universal.

reviews.rationale: The claim is universal ('every single AI app'). Anthropic's early-2025 economics support it for Claude. Under the contract's maker-level reading, Gamma's self-reported profitability in 2025 is one app whose price covered its maker's costs, which contradicts the universal. The result depends on that reading, and on accepting Gamma's unaudited disclosure as the contract permits.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words; 'it' refers to OpenAI in context.

semantics.note: Narrowing 'anybody' to compute providers fits the context. The CoreWeave terms are an illustration, not the claim.

contract.note: Reading 'cannot afford' as lacking funds from any source is the ordinary meaning. His context (revenue vs commitments) hints at a narrower reading about revenue, but the words say more than that. The result depends on this choice.

evidence.note: FT-verified 2025 financials: OpenAI paid about $17.2B to Microsoft for cloud and R&D in 2025.
Reuters: SoftBank completed its $40B investment, with the final $22-22.5B sent in late December 2025. Shows capital was available; timing is right at the post date.
OpenAI spent 2.5x its revenue. This bears on the narrower revenue reading, not on its ability to pay.

reviews.rationale: On the plain reading, OpenAI could afford to pay providers in 2025. It paid Microsoft about $17.2B and had tens of billions in committed investor capital, including SoftBank's final tranche in late December. Revenue did not cover costs, but that is a different claim. The CoreWeave payment terms were not confirmed and do not change the result.
